change: Its source becomes dead wasps at the bug extractor (the direct drop was removed, D22); its job is the wasp-thorn outfit, the first of the three thorn outfits. The smoker's recipe uses one today and could take bug leather for the bellows instead.
reason: The thorn outfits (August 2026) sting whoever hits the wearer, so each needs its family's real sting.

name: Water Beetle Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A diving beetle's shell is beetle chitin; the diving helmet it lined is gone.

name: Water Bug Venom Gland
reason: A seventh venom for one swamp boss; the antivenom still cures its bite, and six venoms cover the potion strengths.

name: Black Widow Silk
change: Rename 'Black Widow Silk': from black widows at the bug extractor or cut from their webs, in Spider Vale East; the widow's armour, the top stealth outfit, is made from it.
reason: The stealth outfits end in the widow's armour (outfit roster), and black widow silk is famously strong.

name: Wheat
reason: The Locust Farmland's crop (D42); the mill turns it into flour, and cutting it down gives straw.

name: Whirligig Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A whirligig beetle's shell is beetle chitin.

name: Black Widow Venom
reason: The strongest of the six venoms, from black widows in Spider Vale East; it makes the strongest antivenom and the strongest Bug Bomb.

name: Spider Fang
change: Rename 'Spider Fang': from the big spiders of Spider Vale at the bug extractor; it is the blade of the Spider-Fang Dagger, the top dagger. Huntsman and matron fangs merge in.
reason: The table keeps one spider-fang dagger, and 'wolf fang' read as a mammal's tooth.

name: Wood
reason: Chopped from trees everywhere; planks, torches, tool handles and early building, and the furnace burns it into coal.

name: Yellow Dye
reason: One of the four basic dyes, made from dandelions and sold by the Weaver (D44).

name: Cobalt Ore
change: A new ore mined with the steel pickaxe in the deep rock zones, often beside silver; its examine text tells how its pink crust ('cobalt bloom') led real prospectors to silver. Crushed and washed like every ore (D26), it goes into cobalt steel.
reason: Every pickaxe rung must open an ore (P20), and cobalt is one of the two new ores the owner accepted (D61).

name: Crushed Cobalt Ore
change: The rock crusher's output for cobalt ore; washed at the sluice next.
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Washed Cobalt Ore
change: The sluice's output for cobalt; the forge adds it to steel bars to make cobalt steel bars, the way washed tin joins copper bars to make bronze (no plain cobalt bar).
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26), and cobalt's only job is mixing into steel.

name: Cobalt Steel Bar
change: Made at the forge from steel bars and washed cobalt ore; the seventh tool rung and the top rung of metal armour (the cobalt-steel pickaxe and outfit).
reason: P20 and D61 put cobalt steel on the seventh rung, and armour stops there.

name: Tungsten Ore
change: Mined with the cobalt-steel pickaxe in the deepest rock; it glows sky-blue under the UV lamp, as the real ore scheelite does. Crushed and washed, it goes into tungsten steel.
reason: The eighth rung needs its ore (P20), and its glow gives the UV lamp its job.

name: Crushed Tungsten Ore
change: The rock crusher's output for tungsten ore; washed at the sluice next.
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Washed Tungsten Ore
change: The sluice's output for tungsten; the forge adds it to steel bars to make tungsten steel bars, the way cobalt makes cobalt steel (no plain tungsten bar).
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26), and tungsten's job is mixing into steel (D69).

name: Tungsten Steel Bar
change: Made at the forge from steel bars and washed tungsten ore; the eighth tool rung (the tungsten-steel pickaxe) and the rock drill's bits.
reason: The top tool rung is tungsten steel (D61, renamed in D69).

name: Cotton
change: A later crop grown outside the village (for example in the Locust Farmland); the spinning wheel spins it into cotton thread and the loom weaves cotton cloth, for finer clothes than roughspun ones. Its plant and seed come with the crops.
reason: D15 decided cotton as a cloth source, a later crop; the owner leans to keeping it for finer clothes (2026-10-01).

name: Netting
reason: One woven mesh is enough: the fly netting (fine netting) and the heavy netting are what net runs are strung from, woven at the loom in one step, and the cast net is woven from cord.

name: Bone Meal
change: The mill grinds bones into bone meal in one step, a fertiliser that raises yield (D42); how strong it is next to compost is set with the fertiliser design (section 06).
reason: It gives bones, the one kept remains that drop an item, a real use, as Stardew's bone mill does, and uses the mill P11 already plans.

name: Anchor
reason: An old ship's anchor is a salvaged relic that suits a dock or a fisher's plot; it has its own look and stands twice in the village.

name: Ant Colony Chart
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: A chart of an ant colony's castes is bug-science décor for the myrmecologist's building and an ant keeper's home, the game's own kind of art; it stands in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Ant Eggs
change: Becomes the egg stage of an ant colony's brood, shown in the nest's panel and taken or moved like fly and wasp eggs; the loose pick-up (which gives an 'Ant Egg' item) goes.
reason: Ants lay eggs rather than drop them (D18), and ranching ants (D67) needs ant brood to work like every other nursery.

name: Antenna
reason: Nothing in the game receives a signal, so it has no job; the weather board covers forecasts. Unplaced.

name: Anvil
change: Makes every metal tool, weapon and armour rung, copper to tungsten steel; the tools, weapons and armour the forge makes today move here. Stays in the blacksmith's smithy in the village, usable and not takeable (D55).
reason: Anvil and forge both make tools today, split by tier for no reason a player can see; one station for metal gear is clearer.

name: Apple Crate
change: Stays as market and orchard dressing (a townsperson's crate of apples) but can't be broken for apples and wood.
reason: All ten stand in the village, where players can't break or take the townspeople's things (D41); apples come from the orchard.

name: Aquarium
reason: A fish tank suits a player who fishes, and fishing starts in the village (D51); a distinct piece, placed once in the village.

name: Armchair
reason: The living-room armchair, crafted at the sawmill; placed in the village and the Bee Meadow.

name: Wingback Armchair
reason: The fancy armchair, part of the bought-later fancy set (D19); three stand in the village.

name: Autonet
change: Give it the accepted job: it draws in bugs from the area just ahead of it, holds more than a net run and stops when full, and the player empties it by hand (P3). Today it only stores items.
reason: The autonet is the decided machine catcher (D34), but in the prototype it is a plain storage box.

name: Awning
reason: A cloth awning gives shopfronts, stalls and players' houses character for little cost; the weaver's cloth goods.

name: Bait Basket
reason: Its picture is a basket of worms, and there are no worms (D64); the bait dish covers bait. Unplaced.

name: Bait Station
change: Becomes the Bait Dish (P4): a dish on a short post that holds one bait, such as rotting fruit for flies, a carcass for carrion beetles or something sweet for wasps (bees come too), and draws the species that like it from nearby to a catcher beside it.
reason: Bait in a dish beside a catcher is the accepted design (P4), and its picture is already a dish on a post; two stand in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Bar Cart
reason: A drinks trolley repeats the wine rack while drinks don't exist yet; unplaced filler.

name: Barrel
change: Give it a workbench recipe (wood); it has none today.
reason: Cheap storage and the most used town prop (34 placed), a second look beside the crate; no one can make or buy it yet.

name: Basket
reason: A small lidded store (D27), cheap and early; placed in the village and the Bee Meadow.

name: Bathtub
reason: A bathroom is its own kind of room, and this is its piece; four stand in the village.

name: Beach Umbrella
reason: World-only, unplaced and without a job; docks, boats and nets dress the coast.

name: Basic Bed
reason: The first bed: sleeping in it sets where you wake, and players may sleep only in their own or an abandoned bed (D45).

name: Canopy Bed
reason: A second premium bed doing the same job as the fancy bed; unplaced. Its recipe slot at the carpenter's passes to the four-poster bed.

name: Fancy Bed
change: Rename 'Four-Poster Bed' (its picture has four tall posts); the one premium bed, its recipe sold by the carpenter in the canopy bed's place.
reason: One fancy bed is enough, and this one already stands three times (village and Bee Meadow).

name: Floral Bed
reason: Part of the floral set, eight pieces that repeat the basic furniture with flowers painted on; no one sells the set, none is placed and none has a sprite.

name: Stone Slab Bed
reason: A stone copy of the bed; unplaced and without a sprite.

name: Large Bee Station
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: One of the two hive boxes the owner chose when the four hive sizes were collapsed (2026-07-06); Maren sells it.

name: Small Bee Station
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: The other hive box the owner kept (2026-07-06); Maren sells it and four stand in her apiary.

name: Bee Waterer
change: Merge into the Butterfly Water Dish (the birdbath's new form); its shallow pebble-and-water tub is the right picture for that dish, and bees drink from it too.
reason: Two water dishes for pollinators would be one job twice; the one in Maren's apiary becomes the dish.

name: Basic Beehive
reason: The owner replaced the hive tiers with the two bee stations (2026-07-06); the four in the village never come alive, and become small bee stations.

name: Deluxe Beehive
reason: Replaced by the large bee station (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Large Beehive
reason: Replaced by the bee stations (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Medium Beehive
reason: Replaced by the bee stations (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Maren (Beekeeper)
reason: The Bee Meadow's townsperson and the heart of the honey trade: she sells the bee stations, smoker, suit and calm spray and buys honey, comb and wax.

name: Beetle Eggs
reason: The carrion beetle's egg stage in its nursery, shown in the panel and taken or moved like other brood.

name: Beetle Grubs
reason: The carrion beetle's grub stage in its nursery.

name: Beetle Pupae
reason: The carrion beetle's pupa stage in its nursery.

name: Wooden Bench
reason: The town's outdoor seat (ten placed), an early craft at the workbench.

name: Marble Bench
reason: A second stone bench; the stone bench covers it. Unplaced, no sprite.

name: Padded Bench
reason: A cushioned copy of the wooden bench; unplaced.

name: Stone Bench
reason: The one stone garden seat, from the stonemason.

name: Birdbath
change: Becomes the Butterfly Water Dish (D66): a shallow dish of damp sand and pebbles set on the ground (the bee waterer's tub is the picture to use), whose examine text says butterflies really gather on damp ground to drink water and minerals. Its stonecutter recipe carries over; the two in the village are swapped.
reason: Birds are gone, and the owner settled this misfit's replacement (D66).

name: Brann (Blacksmith)
reason: The village blacksmith sells bars and metal gear and buys bars; the village's anvil, forge and furnace stand at his smithy (D55).

name: Rowboat
reason: Deep water always takes a boat (D51); the fisherman sells it and four are placed.

name: Bookshelf
change: Drop the books-only rule so it stores anything.
reason: Recipe books are learned, not carried (D26), so no book item exists and today it accepts nothing; five are placed.

name: Mahogany Bookcase
change: The fancy-set bookcase (D19); drop the books-only rule as for the bookshelf.
reason: It stands four times in the village but, like the bookshelf, accepts nothing today.

name: Vine Bookshelf
reason: Part of the floral set that repeats the basic furniture with flowers; unobtainable, unplaced, no sprite.

name: Brick Pile
reason: Building-site dressing for the stonemason's yard (three placed); cheap and makes the yard read as a yard.

name: Broken Fence
reason: The ruin look for abandoned farms and a small find; with the weathered picket gone it is the one ruined fence. Unplaced so far.

name: Bug Dealer
reason: Buys live and dead bugs at the same price (D37) and sells a few back; the player's first coins come from here, and he teaches the bug dishes.

name: Bug Extractor
change: Stand one in the village at the Bug Dealer's, usable and not takeable (D55), so carcasses can be turned into chitin, leather and the rest from the start; players buy or make their own later (D37).
reason: It turns every carcass into materials (D18) yet stands only in a test zone and can't be obtained.

name: Bug Terrarium (small)
change: Merge into the specimen case: its picture (a pinned beetle under glass on a stand) becomes the specimen case's picture, and the four in the village become specimen cases.
reason: Its picture is a pinned specimen, not a living tank, and the big terrarium is the living display.

name: Bug Terrarium
reason: A glass tank for a living bug display, a keeper's showpiece and the game's own kind of décor; the Ecologist sells its recipe (D26).

name: Bunk Bed
reason: Two sleeping places in one bed's space, so friends sharing a house each have a bed to wake in.

name: Buoy
reason: Water dressing that marks channels and moorings (two in the Bee Meadow's inlet); world-only.

name: Marble Bust
reason: The stone statue's picture is already a bust on a pedestal, so a second bust repeats it; no sprite, unplaced.

name: Caterpillars
reason: The caterpillar stage in the milkweed nursery; from there caterpillars go out into the world (D38).

name: Chrysalis
change: Leaves the milkweed's panel and becomes a world object: the chrysalis a caterpillar forms on a plant or fence out in the world, which later opens into a butterfly (and can be collected for the Ecologist, P9).
reason: The nursery holds only eggs and young caterpillars; the chrysalis forms out in the world (D38).

name: Butterfly Eggs
reason: The egg stage in the milkweed nursery.

name: Display Cabinet
reason: It stores exactly what the cupboard does (twelve spaces) and looks much the same; the one in the village becomes a cupboard.

name: Campfire
reason: The camp light and the first cooking step, one dish at a time, before the wood stove and the range; made at the workbench from the start.

name: Campfire Spit
reason: A second campfire for the same job; its two in the mining camp become campfires.

name: Candelabra
reason: A table light of beeswax candles; the blacksmith sells its recipe (D26). Candles are neither oil lamps nor magic.

name: Candle
reason: The smallest light, made from beeswax and fibre (D31), a use for the beekeeper's wax; the general store sells its recipe.

name: Beeswax Candle
reason: The candle is already made of beeswax (D31); the two in Maren's cottage become candles. No sprite.

name: Wynn (Carpenter)
reason: Sells furniture and building recipes and planks; the village's workbench and sawmill stand at his shop (D55).

name: Cat Statue
reason: A statue, and statues and remains are fine (D66); one stands in the village.

name: Cauldron
change: The potion station (P16, D54): give it the starting potions (healing potion, antivenom, the salve, venom resistance, night sight) and stand one in the village at a shop, usable and not takeable (D55); the Ecologist's house suits it, since the potions come from bug venom and study.
reason: The owner named it the potion station, but it makes nothing today and stands in no real zone.

name: Cave Moss
reason: Floor greenery that softens the first mine (304 placed), and a grotto décor a player can pick up and place.

name: Centipede Eggs
reason: The centipede's egg stage; centipedes count as bugs (D64), and real centipede mothers guard their eggs.

name: Young Centipedes
reason: The centipede's young stage in its nursery.

name: Cushioned Chair
reason: Looks and works like the fancy chair (both purple cushioned chairs); unplaced.

name: Fancy Chair
reason: The fancy-set chair, bought later (D19); two stand in the village.

name: Floral Chair
reason: Part of the floral set that repeats the basic furniture; unobtainable, unplaced, no sprite.

name: Wooden Chair
reason: The basic chair, an early craft (ten placed).

name: Chaise Lounge
reason: A near-duplicate of the sofa; unplaced.

name: Small Chest
reason: A one-square box with the same twelve spaces as the crate and barrel; the one in the Bee Meadow becomes a crate.

name: Iron Chest
change: Give it an anvil recipe (it has none); with the trunk cut it is the biggest chest.
reason: The strong late chest, but nothing makes it today (the blacksmith's 'Iron Chest' on sale is chest armour, not this).

name: Mossy Chest
reason: A chest found in ruins and caves with loot inside when first opened, a reward for exploring; not craftable.

name: Wooden Chest
change: Give it its workbench recipe (wood); it has none, so the standard chest can't be made today.
reason: The standard home chest (24 spaces); D37 asks that everything in the game be obtainable.

name: Chisel Bench
reason: Dressing that makes the stonemason's workshop read as one (one placed); village dressing, not sold.

name: Clay Block
change: Clay pockets in the dirt masses, dug with the shovel; clay fires into bricks at the furnace, so brick walls come from clay rather than from stone.
reason: It gives digging through dirt something to find besides stone and ore, and bricks really are fired clay; today nothing uses clay.

name: Clothing Rack
reason: A rail of outfits for the weaver's shop (two placed) and a dressing room; it holds clothes.

name: Coal Bin
change: Holds coal only, a fuel store beside the furnace.
reason: The furnace and forge burn coal, so a coal store earns its place beside them; today it is a prop with no use (six placed).

name: Coat Rack
reason: A third clothes store beside the dresser and wardrobe; unplaced.

name: Coffee Table
reason: The living room's low table, from the carpenter's basic book.

name: Collection Tray
reason: Placed catchers hold their own catch until emptied (P3), so a tray to gather it has no job; the three in the village go.

name: Marble Column
reason: The pillars of the Mayor's hall (four placed), a grand building piece from the stonemason.

name: Compost Bin
change: Two sizes, as D19 decided: the compost bin and a large compost bin that holds more scraps (and so breeds more flies).
reason: Scraps become compost to sell and to fertilise with (D37) while flies breed in the warm rot, the start of most fly farms.

name: Cooking Pot
reason: Cooking runs campfire, then wood stove, then range, each cooking more dishes at once; a separate pot repeats the campfire. Unplaced.

name: Cot
reason: The tent covers sleeping in camp and the basic bed is the first home bed; the general store sells the tent in its place. One placed in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Kitchen Counter
reason: The kitchen worktop (fourteen placed).

name: Marble Counter
reason: The fancy-set counter (four placed).

name: Cow Skull
reason: Old remains are fine (D66); dry-ground dressing and a find.

name: Crate
change: Give it a workbench recipe (wood); it has none today.
reason: The cheapest store and a village starter (42 placed), but no one can make or buy it yet.

name: Cupboard
reason: Kitchen storage (three placed).

name: Stone Cupboard
reason: A stone copy of the cupboard; unplaced, no sprite.

name: Dead Bush
reason: The owner cut it in the June prune (D26); the 122 on the Bee Meadow's dry ground go when that zone is redesigned (D53), replaced by living dry-ground plants.

name: Writing Desk
reason: A study desk with drawers, a small store (three placed).

name: Stone Desk
reason: A stone copy of the desk; unplaced, no sprite.

name: Carved Dining Table
reason: The fancy-set dining table (two placed).

name: Dirt Block
reason: The dirt masses of the ant zones and the surface, holding stone and ore cores so digging finds things (51,777 placed).

name: Dock Planks
change: Laid on water to make docks and footbridges, the one floor that crosses water.
reason: Water divides the map (D51) and docks already dress the shores, but these planks can't yet be laid on water; unplaced.

name: Iron Door
change: The strong door for barns and pens: bugs that can break wood can't break iron (the fence materials apply to doors too); needs a side-facing sprite so it turns to fit its wall (D45).
reason: A pen's door has to hold what its walls hold; unplaced today.

name: Simple Door
change: Rename 'Wooden Door', the standard one-square door (58 placed); add a side-facing sprite so it turns to fit the wall it is placed in (D45).
reason: Doors that turn to fit their wall are decided (D45), and this is the door every house uses.

name: Wooden Door (two wide)
change: Rename 'Barn Door': the two-square door, wide enough to drag a big bug through into a barn or pen (P15); side-facing sprite too (D45).
reason: Big bugs are dragged home (P15), and a one-square door is too narrow for them; unplaced today, so it gets a real job.

name: Dress Form
reason: The mannequins replaced it in the weaver's display (D27); unplaced.

name: Dresser
reason: Stores clothes and outfits (six placed); the carpenter's basic book.

name: Carved Dresser
reason: The fancy-set dresser (D19; two placed).

name: Floral Dresser
reason: Part of the floral set that repeats the basic furniture; unobtainable, unplaced, no sprite.

name: Fish Drying Rack
reason: Fishing-hamlet dressing (three in the Bee Meadow); world-only.

name: Dye Vat
change: Dyes cloth and cloth outfits with a dye (D44's recolouring); making the dyes moves to a new dye station (the mortar and pestle, added below). Stays at the weaver's in the village.
reason: The owner asked for dye vats to dye cloth and for a separate station to make the dyes (2026-06-28); today the vat only makes dyes.

name: Easel
reason: A painter's easel with a canvas, the one painting until things can hang on walls; it stands in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Dr. Vesper (Ecologist)
reason: Opens the Ecology tab, gives the ecology quests and sells recipes for his house's pieces (D40, P9).

name: Electric Heater
reason: Nothing in the game is cold, so a heater does nothing; the one in the Modern Wares showroom goes.

name: Fabric Bolt
reason: Dressing for the weaver's shop (two placed) and a craft-room décor.

name: Wooden Fence Corner
reason: Fences built from posts and rails join into corners on their own (P5).

name: Electric Fence
change: Rebuilt as a powered wire fence of posts and rails (P5): while powered it shocks bugs back so they leave it alone; without power it is the weakest fence. Modern Wares sells it.
reason: No material may be best against everything (P5), and the power cost and weak unpowered state keep this one honest; unplaced today.

name: Iron Fence
change: Rebuilt as posts and iron rails (P5): wasps can't scrape it and beetles can't shove it, but acid-spraying ants eat through iron; numbers set when the ecology is tuned.
reason: P5 gives each fence material its own strengths and weak spot; 95 stand in the village.

name: Picket Fence
change: Rebuilt as posts and pickets that join on their own (P5); wood, so it resists bugs the way the rail fence does.
reason: The village's white fence (273 placed) and the cosy look players will want; same material as the rail fence, a different look.

name: Weathered Picket Fence
reason: An aged look of the picket fence that would need its own full set of joining pieces (P5); the broken fence covers ruins. Its 161 placements (village and Bee Meadow) become pickets or broken fences.

name: Stone Fence
change: Rebuilt as a low stone wall that joins on its own (P5): scraping wasps can't hurt it and it holds big shovers well, but it is slow and costly to build and not the answer to everything (D36); numbers set when the ecology is tuned.
reason: The heavy fence material; unplaced in the real zones today.

name: Wooden Fence
change: Becomes P5's post-and-rail fence: place a post, drag to another and rails fill the run; pieces join on their own and gates fit in. Wasps scrape wood for nest paper, so it is weak against them (P5).
reason: The accepted fence rebuild (P5); its picture is already a post and rail, and it is the most placed fence (326).

name: Fireplace
change: Give it light like the campfire; the indoor hearth that lights a room.
reason: A hearth with a fire in its picture gives no light today; two are placed.

name: Fish Crate
change: Holds the catch only (fish, crayfish and crabs), the dock's store beside the produce crate for crops.
reason: Two small food crates with one job would be duplicates; giving each its own contents keeps both (fifteen fish crates are placed).

name: Cael (Fisherman)
change: Place him at his house by the village lake (D51); he sells the fishing rods, the fish trap and the rowboat, not the decorative pole and net, and takes fish in trade (P19). Bait is bug meat or a small bug the player already has.
reason: Fishing starts in the village with him (D51), but he stands in no zone, and he sells a decorative pole as if it were a rod.

name: Drying Net
reason: A net drying on a frame, dock dressing and fishing-plot décor that the fisherman sells.

name: Fishing Pole
change: Merge into the first fishing rod (the cane rod added with the tools): the fisherman already sells this at 40 as if it were a rod, and its picture is a plain pole.
reason: A decorative pole beside a real rod would confuse players.

name: Fly Eggs
reason: The fly's egg stage in the compost bin's brood, the start of every fly farm.

name: Fly Maggots
reason: The fly's maggot stage in the compost bin.

name: Fly Netting
change: Becomes the fine netting of a net run (P3): strung between net posts the way rails go between fence posts, small flyers blunder in and hang there, a few at a time; taking it down gives back the netting (P4).
reason: Net runs are the accepted placed catcher for flyers, built on these pieces; sixteen stand in the village.

name: Fly Pupae
reason: The fly's pupa stage, kept for compost-bin flies (2026-07-17).

name: Forge
change: Makes the alloy bars only (bronze, steel, cobalt steel, tungsten steel); its tools and weapons move to the anvil. Stays in the village smithy, usable and not takeable (D55).
reason: Forge and anvil both make tools, and forge and furnace both make bars; mixing metals into alloys is a real separate step, so each of the three gets one job.

name: Formicarium
change: Becomes the ant keeper's nest box: an ant colony lives in it the way bees take a bee station, so ants can be ranched (D67); the myrmecologist sells it. Needs a sprite.
reason: Ranching ants is one of the named ways to play (D67), and a formicarium really is a keeper's ant nest; today it is a display with no job (one in the Ant Tunnels).

name: Fountain
reason: The village square's centrepiece (three placed), the grand water feature.

name: Refrigerator
change: A powered food chest that holds much more than a crate (food doesn't spoil, P16); in the village it stands only in the Mayor's house, which has power (D56).
reason: Without spoiling a fridge is only a food chest, so power has to buy it something; five stand around the village today.

name: Furnace

reason: P20 gives platinum this job, and without a store a solar farm has no power at night.

name: Mill
change: Grinds grain into flour and corn into cornmeal, one step each (P11); it stands in the Locust Farmland's town, where the wheat is, and players buy their own later. The General Store sells flour and cornmeal so village cooks can start sooner.
reason: The mill is one of the accepted simple stations (P11), and flour is added with the materials; no mill exists.

name: Fruit Press
change: Presses fruit into juice and sunflower or pumpkin seeds into oil, one step each (P11); it stands in Maren's brewing room in the Bee Meadow beside the keg, and players buy their own later.
reason: The press is one of the accepted simple stations (P11), and none exists.

name: Mortar and Pestle (dye station)
change: Grinds flowers, leaves and roots into dyes in one step (P11); the four dye recipes move here from the dye vat, and it stands at the weaver's in the village.
reason: The owner asked for a separate station to make dyes, with the dye vat dyeing cloth (2026-06-28), and P11 names the dye station; none exists.

name: Powered stations (the family)
change: The slow processing stations get powered versions that work faster and take more jobs at once: furnace, sawmill, spinning wheel, loom, mill, fruit press, bug extractor, honey extractor and compost bin; the hand stations (workbench, anvil, stonecutter) don't. Players meet them where generators can be bought (D55).
reason: Powered versions of stations are decided (D55), but which ones is still open; the slow machines are where power saves real waiting.

name: Myrmecologist
change: The ant specialist who sells from a wooden building at the Ant Tunnels' entrance (its sign is placed): ant-keeping goods such as the formicarium, quests, and a board of retrieval jobs, some out of reach at first (D52).
reason: The myrmecologist is decided (2026-07-07, D52), but no townsperson exists for the role.

name: Black Ant Nest
change: Rename it 'Black Ant Nest' and make it the black ants' nursery, working like the wasp nest: open it to take eggs, larvae and pupae, and breaking it kills the brood instead of dropping ant eggs. It needs a picture (none exists) and belongs in the Ant Tunnels' brood chamber, which has no nest today, and in the Ant Colony. The fire ants nest in the ant mound, so each species keeps a nest of its own (a nest two species share ends up holding only one of them).
reason: The game's data already makes it the ants' nest, but it has no picture and sits only in a test zone, and ants lay eggs rather than drop them (D18).

name: Wild Bee Hive
reason: The honeybees' wild home, where bee colonies start (5 in the Bee Meadow); chopping one for its honeycomb destroys that colony's home, a real choice between honey now and bees later.

name: Hornet Nest
change: Keep it as the hornets' own nest, working like the wasp nest: open it to take the brood, and breaking it kills the brood instead of dropping paper and larvae (that drop was already taken off the wasp nest, D23). It needs a picture (none exists) and a place wherever the hornet ends up once it has its real species name (the zone designs put hornets in the Hilltop Meadow).
reason: Hornets need a nest of their own, since a nest shared with the wasps ends up holding only one of the two, but today it has no picture and sits in no real zone.

name: Barrel Cactus
reason: A third cactus with no job beside the saguaro (which gives wood) and the prickly pear (fruit); it only drops itself and sits in no zone.

name: Prickly Pear
change: Rename it 'Prickly Pear' and give it a harvest: picking it gives prickly pears, a desert fruit to eat or sell, with the usual chance of a pad to plant (D24). Its home is Scorpion Rocks, the desert zone, and it is the cochineal's host plant (its own row).
reason: Today it is named like a label ('Cactus Prickly') and only drops itself, while a real edible cactus gives the desert something to forage.

name: Driftwood
reason: Sea-worn wood on the Bee Meadow's coast (21 pieces): wood without trees, and a sign that the sea is near.

name: Duckweed
change: Grow it on the swamps' still water and let it drop itself (today it drops fibre), so players can spread it to other ponds, where a covering of it means far fewer mosquitoes.
reason: Real studies find that a duckweed cover sharply cuts how many mosquito larvae survive beneath it, a true lever for the mosquito zone (plants steer bugs, P8); today it sits in no zone and does nothing.

name: Amethyst Cluster
change: Rename it 'Amethyst Cluster': it drops quartz, the one crystal item, and its examine text says amethyst is purple quartz. It keeps the stone-pickaxe gate it has today and stays the caves' crystal dressing (19 in the first mine).
reason: Its picture is already purple amethyst, a real gem players know and the stone that lines many real geodes, while 'crystal' says nothing about what it is.

name: Large Amethyst Cluster
change: Rename it 'Large Amethyst Cluster': the rare big find of the deeper caves, giving three quartz and needing a better pickaxe than the small cluster (the copper one, as today).
reason: Like a big tree that needs a better axe, a big cluster behind a better pick is a reward worth coming back for; it sits in no zone yet.

name: Fallen Oranges
reason: A still picture of oranges that only the preview tools draw; orange trees drop real oranges that rot where they fall, and the fallen-apples picture is cut the same way.

name: Cornflower
change: Rename it 'Cornflower' (new art follows the name). It stays the common meadow flower that bees and butterflies feed on (177 placed, most in the Bee Meadow and the village), and its flowers become the blue dye's own ingredient, as poppies make red, dandelions yellow and clover green (today any three flowers make blue).
reason: Examining a thing shows its real biology, which a plain 'Blue Flower' can't do, and cornflower petals really were used for blue colour.

name: Bluebell
change: Rename it 'Bluebell' (from 'Flower Bluebell'), make it a flower bees feed on, and let it carpet the shady floor of the Millipede Forest.
reason: Bluebells are the real flower of old woodland and an early food for bees, giving the forest a look of its own; today it feeds nothing and sits in no zone.

name: Foxglove
reason: A second woodland flower doing the bluebell's job; it feeds nothing and sits in no zone.

name: Buttercup
change: Rename it 'Buttercup' (new art follows the name); it stays a common meadow flower that bees and butterflies feed on (158 placed).
reason: A plain 'Yellow Flower' has no real biology to show when examined; buttercups are the real yellow flower of meadows, and the dandelion already makes the yellow dye.

name: Grapevine
reason: It shows grapes in its picture but drops only fibre and sits in no zone; grapes would be a new crop for some zone's design, not a stray wild vine.

name: Fallen Log
reason: Rotting deadfall is where real millipedes, beetles and centipedes shelter, so it suits the forests as cover, wood and now and then wood grubs (2 in the Bee Meadow today); its picture can carry the bracket fungus, which is cut.

name: Giant Milkweed
reason: A bigger copy of the milkweed that isn't a butterfly nursery itself and sits in no zone; the milkweed does the job.

name: Morning Glory
reason: A blue vine in no zone; the cornflower and the bluebell already cover blue flowers.

name: Moss Clump
reason: Damp ground cover for cave mouths, pool banks and forest floors that breaks for fibre (31 in the first mine); the clubmoss is cut in its favour.

name: Bracket Fungus
reason: A woody shelf fungus that nobody eats, blocks players, needs an axe and sits in no zone; the forest potions it was meant for are gone (P16), and the chanterelle covers forest foraging.

name: Inkcap
change: Make it the ingredient of a new black dye at the dye station (the mortar and pestle). Pick it by hand (today it needs an axe and blocks players), stop bees and butterflies feeding on it (mushrooms make no nectar), and grow it in grassy places as well as the Ant Tunnels, where the ants already eat it.
reason: Inkcaps really melt into a black ink that people once wrote with, and the game has no black dye yet (only red, yellow, blue and green).

name: Morel
change: Follow-up: remove it from the worker and scout ants' food lists in the species data.
reason: A second prized forest mushroom beside the chanterelle, which is kept for that job (the chanterelle has an item and 4 placed, the morel 1).

name: Coal Deposit
reason: The fuel every furnace and forge burns (steel takes two), found from the village's rock to the mines (2,028 blocks); it stays the wooden pickaxe's ore, so torches and the first smelt never wait on a better tool.

name: Copper Deposit
change: Opened by the stone pickaxe instead of the wooden one (P20: stone reaches copper); common near the surface and in the first mine.
reason: If the wooden pick already mines copper, the stone pick opens nothing new and can be skipped, which the ladder rules out.

name: Tin Deposit
change: Opened by the copper pickaxe instead of the wooden one (P20: copper reaches tin).
reason: Tin is what turns copper into bronze, so it belongs one rung after copper; among the real zones only the first mine holds it (269 blocks).

name: Iron Deposit
change: Opened by the bronze pickaxe instead of the stone one (P20: bronze reaches iron). Iron is the first mine's most common ore today (2,920 blocks there), so the redesigned mine should put copper and tin near the top and iron deeper.
reason: Iron is the ladder's milestone rung, and holding it behind bronze gives copper and tin their reason.

name: Silver Deposit
change: A deep reward, opened by the iron pickaxe (today the stone one) and found only deep down: today it is common in the first mine (579 blocks) and the Ant Tunnels (238), and 3 sit on the Bee Meadow's surface. Silver goes to solar panels, contacts, mirrors, jewelry and selling, never tools (P20). Its picture is almost blank.
reason: Silver stays in the world as a valuable deep find (P20), but a stone pick reaches it in the first mine today.

name: Gold Deposit
change: A deep reward, opened by the cobalt-steel pickaxe (today the copper one) beside tungsten, in the deep zones only; today 290 blocks sit in the first mine, 62 in the Ant Tunnels and 2 on the Bee Meadow's surface. Gold goes to connectors, gilding (the gilded-steel outfit), jewelry and selling, never tools or weapons (P20).
reason: Gold stays as a deep reward with real jobs (P20), but a copper pick reaches it in the first mine today.

name: Platinum Deposit
change: The deepest metal, opened by the tungsten-steel pickaxe (today the iron one) and found only in the deepest zones (today 139 blocks sit in the first mine). Platinum goes into the platinum outfit (with steel), selling and a few power recipes, never tools (P20).
reason: The top pickaxe needs an ore to open, and platinum is the deepest reward the ladder names.

name: Diamond Deposit
change: The rarest gem, opened by the tungsten-steel pickaxe (today the steel one) and found only in the deepest zones (today 82 blocks sit in the first mine); cut and sold or made into jewelry, never tools (D49). Its picture is almost blank.
reason: The gems open in the order of their real hardness (emerald, then ruby and sapphire, then diamond, the hardest), so the hardest stone waits for the hardest pick.

name: Emerald Deposit
change: Keep it as a deep gem, opened by the steel pickaxe (today the copper one) and found in veins in the deep mining zones; it sits in no zone today.
reason: Gems stay as gems to cut, sell and set in jewelry, and emerald is the softest of the four, so it opens first.

name: Ruby Deposit
change: Keep it as a deep gem, opened by the cobalt-steel pickaxe (today the iron one) in the deep mining zones; the only ruby placed today is one block on the Bee Meadow's surface beside two gold blocks, which the redesign should move underground.
reason: Ruby and sapphire are really the same mineral in two colours, harder than emerald and softer than diamond, so they share the rung between.

name: Sapphire Deposit
change: Keep it as a deep gem beside the ruby, opened by the cobalt-steel pickaxe (today the iron one) in the deep mining zones; it sits in no zone today.
reason: Gems stay as gems, and a blue stone beside the red gives miners one more colour to hunt for.

name: Quartz Deposit
change: Rename it 'Quartz Deposit' to match the other ore blocks. It stays an early find for the first pickaxes, as today, and its quartz is cut at the gem cutter and sold. It needs a real picture (today a plain white square).
reason: Quartz is the rock's common mineral and a small early earner for miners, and 'block' hides that it is a find.

name: Pondweed
reason: A second pond plant in no zone; the lily pad, the reeds and the duckweed already cover the water.

name: Rotten Fruit
change: Follow-up: the Ant Tunnels' starting food is two of these, so seed real fallen fruit there instead. The bugs' food lists use 'rotten fruit' as the name for any fruit that has rotted, and that stays.
reason: A still picture of rotting fruit that only the preview tools draw; real fallen fruit already rots where it lands and feeds the flies, while this one, placed as an object, would feed them without ever running out.

name: Sandcastle
reason: A one-off beach prop with no job that drops nothing when broken; the coast already has driftwood, shells and the wrecked boat.

name: Seashell Pile
reason: Old shells on the Bee Meadow's beaches (49 piles) are remains, which the design keeps (D66), and they make the shore read as a shore; the shells they give sell for a little.

name: Wrecked Boat
change: Rename it 'Wrecked Boat' (the picture is a small boat, and 'shipwrecked' describes people), and keep it as a coastal landmark that can hide a found chest, one of the coast's secrets.
reason: A wreck on the shore is a place worth walking to (1 in the Bee Meadow), and wood is a fair reward for breaking it up.

name: Mossy Stump
reason: A mossier copy of the tree stump (which is kept), giving the same wood and placed in no zone.

name: Cobalt Deposit
change: A new ore block opened by the steel pickaxe, found in veins in the deep mining zones and marked by a pink crust ('cobalt bloom'); it drops cobalt ore, which with steel makes the cobalt-steel rung.
reason: The ladder's seventh rung needs cobalt (P20, D61), and the game has none.

name: Tungsten Deposit
change: A new ore block opened by the cobalt-steel pickaxe, in the deepest mining zones; its ore glows sky-blue under the UV lamp and goes into tungsten steel, the top rung.
reason: The ladder's top rung is tungsten steel (D61, D69), and the game has no tungsten.

name: Farm Store Keeper (western town)
change: A townsperson of the small western-style town in the Locust Farmland who sells wheat seeds (D42) and the larger sprinklers (D56) and takes crops in trade.
reason: The western town needs townspeople of its own (D42), and the design already gives it wheat seeds and the larger sprinklers to sell.

name: Electrician (western town)
change: A townsperson of the western town, which has strings of lights and other electric things (D52): sells windmills (a player's own windmill comes only after reaching the Locust Farmland), generators and the powered pump (P22), and builds power parts from the silver, gold and platinum that players bring (P20).
reason: Powered stations arrive where generators can be bought (D55), electronics are bought rather than crafted (D1, D26), and someone has to turn the precious metals into power parts.

name: Mine Shopkeeper
change: The shopkeeper at the first mine's camp: buys raw ore (the village blacksmith takes only bars, D26), sells mining gear such as the prospecting pan (D43), and owns the camp's rock crusher and sluice, which players may use but not take (D44).
reason: The design puts the real mining gear and the ore trade at the mine (D20, D26), and no shop exists there yet.

name: Bug Vacuum
change: Kept as D12 decided, in the powered tiers: a backpack suction catcher held like a tool that pulls the small bugs in a cone ahead of you into its hold, several at a time, and holds a small load before you empty it. Small bugs only (the nets' size rule, P3); the quick way to gather a fly farm's harvest.
reason: The owner kept it (D12) and nothing later dropped it; real entomologists catch insects with suction samplers, and it is the handheld cousin of the autonet.

name: Grappling Hook
change: Kept (D12) with a new job: thrown onto a post, tree or rock across a gap you can't walk across, such as a ravine or a rock ledge in the rock zones, it pulls you over. Not water: deep water always takes a boat (D51). Where such gaps go is set with the world design.
reason: The owner kept it for crossing deep water, but D51 made deep water boat-only, so it needs another gap to cross; if the world has none, it goes back to him rather than disappearing.

name: Dredge
change: Keep for later (D14): set on a lake or river and worked with its hose, it lifts ordinary sand, clay and bits of ore from the bed, the prospecting pan's big brother, in the weaker-to-stronger tiers D14 describes; its old special outputs (silt, sunken logs) stay cut.
reason: The owner gave its design in D14; with the silt items cut it still has a job, turning water into a source of building sand, clay and a little ore.

name: Bee smokers (the whole family)
change: Three smokers, as D12 decided: the bee smoker for honeybees, then two stronger ones that calm fiercer bees for longer (wild colonies, and the killer bees the thorn line's top outfit names). No metal names; each is a better smoker, not a metal rung.
reason: D12 wants beekeeping tools that grow with fiercer bees; the table keeps only the first.

name: Role and legendary outfits (the roster)
change: Not judged here: they are judged in the outfit roster with §08. The two approved bug outfits (fire ant, black ant) stay, and the alchemist's robe D47 asks for is the roster's healer's garb.
reason: Without this line the table reads as if every outfit but the metal ladder was dropped, while its materials (fire-ant chitin, black widow silk, wasp stinger) are kept for these very outfits.

name: Outfits and armour (the roster)
change: Decided: one outfit, worn whole, changed any time (D47); each role has its own best set and nothing is the best armour (2026-08-06); non-combat outfits raise a yield or make a job easier (D47); nearly every zone hides an outfit recipe (2026-08-06). Proposed: each outfit suits a trip — armour for its tier plus a bonus or two for that trip, and a visible cost where it is strong; the metal armours stay plain by choice (armour only, heavier ones a little slower), so the role outfits carry the twists; role outfits come back as tougher remakes; the underground fighting armours also carry a small mining-station bonus (a little extra ore at the sluice), as the owner's roster asked. Stealth is built once, as one number — how close a bug has to be to notice you — which each stealth outfit changes its own way (quiet, dark, still, disguise); the catching outfits use the same number, so skittish bugs flee later and curious butterflies come from further. It goes into the shared bug simulation, so those bonuses are marked costly. Damage cuts from different things multiply rather than add, and percentages assume a finer health and damage scale than today's whole numbers.
reason: This answers the roster row above: the owner asked for outfits and armours spread through the game beside the metal ones — bug plate, silk, metals and other materials (2026-10-01) — so the roster is now judged here, row by row. Protections that stop damage reuse how the bee suit already stops stings, a thorn's hit back reuses how hits already work, and bonuses to your own speed, light and tools are cheap to build.

name: Market Gardener's Outfit
change: The farmer's remake (the roster's padded farming outfit): more from each harvest than the Farmer's Outfit, seeds back more often, and some armour. The village General Store, later.
reason: Farming is a role with its own best set (2026-08-06); a remake keeps the job outfit useful as zones get harder.

name: Miner's Gear
change: A lamp in the helmet, so both hands stay free; one pickaxe hit fewer on any block that takes two or more; little armour. The Mine Shopkeeper.
reason: The roster's mining line, first step; mining speed belongs to the pickaxe and the mining outfit, as the owner agreed when the Pickfast Band was cut (2026-10-01).

name: Armoured Mining Gear
change: The same as Miner's Gear, with real armour. A recipe in the Centipede Cavern.
reason: The roster's second mining step.

name: Deep Mining Gear
change: The same again, with the most armour, for the deepest ores. A recipe in the deep Underground River.
reason: The roster's third mining step.

name: Entomologist's Field Coat
change: Skittish bugs such as flies flee from you later (costly: one more use of the stealth number); examining a bug with the magnifying glass opens its facts in half the looks (P8); little armour. The Ecologist.
reason: The roster's scientist among the catching outfits, which the owner wanted to make bugs ignore you and make catching go better (2026-08-06).

name: Butterfly Collector's Whites
change: Curious butterflies and moths come to you from further away (costly: the stealth number turned the other way), and your hand net holds one more of them per swing; little armour. Butterfly Fields.
reason: The roster's butterfly collector; a fuller net catches more of the bugs that are there, never copies of them.

name: Bug Wrangler's Leathers
change: Your bring-it-in-alive tools fill a bug's calm meter faster (if that idea goes ahead), and you walk faster while dragging a bug (costly: dragging isn't built, and it moves a bug in the shared world); little armour. The western town's farm store, for the town's western style.
reason: The roster's one bug wrangler (the owner merged rancher and wrangler): a cowboy for livestock bugs.

name: Village Healer's Garb
change: A 25% chance of an extra potion from each cauldron job; bandages and potions you use on a friend heal 25% more; you hit a little softer. It comes with the cauldron, in the village.
reason: This is the alchemist's robe D47 asks for, which the roster calls the village healer's garb: the basic potion maker.

name: Industrial Chemist's Coat
change: A 25% chance to brew a potion one strength up; acid and spray burns do much less; little armour. A chemist in the western town (a townsperson to add).
reason: The roster's advanced potion maker beside the village healer, as the owner liked: potions made from two angles, the healer's and the chemist's.

name: Ventilated Bee Suit
change: Three layers of mesh, so it stops the same stings as the bee suit and slows you less; a hive-harvest bonus; little armour. The Apiarist at the hilltop apiary (a townsperson to add).
reason: The roster's professional bee suit; real ventilated suits are layered mesh, cool and sting-proof.

name: Armoured Bee Suit
change: The same stings stopped, with real armour and a bigger hive-harvest bonus; slow again, so the ranger outfit stays the quick one. A recipe from the Apiarist.
reason: The owner's armoured bee suit (batch 3); the roster's padded suit folds into these steps.

name: Ranger Outfit
change: Wasp and hornet stings can't get through; quicker and better armoured than the bee suit. The Wasp Thicket's ranger outpost (D72). Needs a list of species on the outfit, a small addition to how the bee suit already stops stings.
reason: The owner's note in batch 3 settles its job.

name: Mantis Armor
change: The attack outfit, made from the chitin of the Locust Farmland's mantis, a rare hunter that comes at the height of a locust swarm: the first hit on a bug at full health does half again as much; quicker than plate, with less armour. A recipe found in the Locust Farmland.
reason: Attack is one of the decided roles and had no outfit. The praying mantis is the ambush hunter, striking from stillness in a fraction of a second.

name: Beetle-Shell Armor
change: The first bug-plate armour, from carrion-beetle chitin: the longer you go unhit, the less damage you take, and each hit takes one step of that away, as Terraria's beetle armour does; hits don't knock you back; heavy. The blacksmith makes it (carrion beetles live in the village, D19). Its design is already picked.
reason: Beetles are a main chitin source in the owner's bug map; bug leather comes first, from flies and butterflies.

name: Black-Ant Armor
change: Ant bites and acid sprays hurt less; a small mining-station bonus. The Ant Colony. Costly option: the colony's black ants take you for one of their own until you strike one.
reason: Made and approved. Some real spiders get into ant nests by smelling like ants.

name: Fire-Ant Armor
change: Fire-ant stings can't get through; the hardest ant armour; a small mining-station bonus. The Deadly Ants outpost.
reason: Made and approved; the key to the fire-ant zone.

name: Scorpion Armor
change: Scorpion stings can't get through, and other venom does less harm; heavy. Scorpion Rocks.
reason: The roster's scorpion set: Scorpion Rocks is the zone of deadly venom.

name: Wasp-Thorn Armor
change: Wasp stingers set in bug leather: a bug that bites or stings you up close takes a hit back, and wasp stings do a little less harm; no help against sprays. The Wasp Thicket.
reason: The roster's thorn line, first step.

name: Hornet-Thorn Armor
change: Stronger thorns, from hornet stingers, and hornet stings do a little less harm. Hilltop Meadow, where the hornets are.
reason: The roster's thorn line, second step.

name: Killer-Bee Thorn Armor
change: The strongest thorns, and bee stings do a little less harm: the bee line's late payoff. Its place waits for killer bees to be placed in a zone.
reason: The roster's third thorn set, back in.

name: Centipede Mail
change: Overlapping centipede plates that move with you: dodges cost less stamina and carry you further; a small mining-station bonus; less armour than plate. The Centipede Cavern.
reason: Agility needs its own set; a centipede's body really is a row of overlapping plates.

name: Cave-Spider Silk Robe
change: Walk a little faster; quiet — bugs notice you only up close while you walk (costly); little armour. A recipe from the Mine Shopkeeper; its silk comes from the small spiders of the Centipede Cavern, since no spiders live in the Mining Camp (D21).
reason: The owner's rule for silk: light, quick, quiet and weak.

name: Shadow Robe
change: A hooded robe of hunting-spider silk: you see a little in the dim (night sight, cheap); at night bugs notice you much later (costly); little armour. Spider Vale West. Its own cut, so a robe dyed black never looks the same.
reason: The owner's example (2026-10-01), and the outfit that helps you see in the dark.

name: Widow's Armor
change: Black-widow silk woven tight: venom does much less harm; light, so it slows you least of the armours. Spider Vale East.
reason: The roster's venom-reducing silk armour. Examine text: tight silk stops fangs going deep, so less venom gets in — in 1887 a doctor even tried layered silk against bullets.

name: Dragonfly Scout Coat
change: Dragonfly-wing membrane over bug leather: walk faster, and you can zoom the view out further than usual; the least armour of its tier. The Deep Swamp.
reason: A scout's outfit for new zones; dragonflies have some of the best eyes of any insect.

name: Brigandine
change: Small steel plates riveted inside a heavy cloth coat: a little less armour than Steel Armor, but quicker. The blacksmith, at steel time.
reason: A real medieval armour, chosen for moving freely; a choice beside plain steel rather than a step above it.

name: Forest Plate
change: Plate in a samurai style, built from rare woods and plant fibre with no bug parts: heavy armour; when you stand still, bugs lose sight of you (costly); slow. The Millipede Forest, the logging zone.
reason: The owner's idea from the roster: a hidden tank that trades speed for defence and cover.

name: Glowworm Armor
change: Armour made from glowworm material (armour, not a glowworm costume): soft light all around you; medium armour; a small mining-station bonus. The Centipede Cavern.
reason: The roster's light armour, briefed as armour like everything else.

name: Glowstick Armor
change: Armour built from glowsticks, made at the workbench: bright light all around you, in the colour you choose; little armour. Plus one try at a stick-figure look made of glowsticks.
reason: The owner wanted to see it (the roster); whether it, the glowworm armour or both stay depends on how they look.

name: Queens' Armor
change: Chitin from both ant queens; its chest stands in a small underground fortress.
reason: A legendary set from the hardest zones (D55), decided 2026-08-06.

name: Spider-Plate Armor
change: The legendary armour of Spider Vale.
reason: A legendary set from the hardest zones (D55). A third legendary is still open.

name: Decorative outfits
change: Festival wear, a pinstripe suit, a beach outfit, the beekeeper's honey-gold formal, moth-wool knits, a traveller's coat, sleepwear and more, some inspired by the bees. They count as decorations on a mannequin on your plot (P26). Designed with the decorations, when the item pass reaches them.
reason: Not on hold (D45); they simply haven't been made yet.

name: Fishing outfits
change: The roster's cave and armoured fishing gear, and perhaps an ultimate one; its basic gear is the Fisherman's Wading Outfit. Designed with fishing (§13).
reason: Fishing is a role with its own best set; its bonuses wait for the fishing design.

name: Industrial farming gear
change: The roster's third farming outfit. Designed with powered farming (P22), since its job depends on the powered tools.
reason: Kept on the roster so it isn't lost.

name: Black Dye
change: The fifth basic dye, ground from inkcap mushrooms at the dye station; sold by the Weaver like the other four.
reason: Dark cloth outfits need black, and inkcaps really dissolve into a black ink people once wrote with.

name: Fish (the catch)
change: A handful of real freshwater fish, each sized to one of the three rods: for example perch and carp in the village lake, trout in the rivers, pike as the big lake catch, and the blind cave fish of the Underground River. Sold, cooked or kept in the aquarium; crayfish and crabs come in the fish trap. The list is settled with §13.
reason: The rods, the fish dishes and the trap all need something to catch, and every creature is a real species (D39).

name: Cochineal
change: A new bug: a tiny scale insect farmed on prickly pears in Scorpion Rocks. It barely moves, so it lives in the plant's own view like the aphids (D46), outside the bug simulation; picked off and crushed into crimson dye.
reason: Real: cochineal has been farmed on prickly pear for its red since at least the second century BC — bug farming for colour. A new species is the owner's call (new bugs are welcome if the balance holds, 2026-09-26).

name: Tough and giant trees
change: Two trees for the forest zones: a tough hardwood (hornbeam, called ironwood for its hard timber) that the iron axe opens, and a giant old-growth oak that an iron or steel axe fells very slowly and the saw much faster; both give hardwood, and both give saplings like every tree (D24).
reason: The axe tiers open tougher trees and the saw makes quick work of big ones (D12, P21, D69); the Millipede Forest's design already calls for great old-growth trunks.

name: Prickly Pear
change: The cactus's fruit, picked in Scorpion Rocks: kompot and juice, and a desert forage to sell.
reason: Prickly pears are a real food, and the desert needs something to forage.

name: Frass
change: The droppings penned bugs leave in their pens (caterpillars and locusts leave the most), shovelled up as a strong fertiliser, and found under the moth roosts in the mines.
reason: §00 promised it; it is the bug farm's own manure, real insect frass is sold as fertiliser today, and it closes the loop in which the garden feeds the bugs and the bugs feed the garden.

name: Moth Roost
change: A cluster of moths resting on a mine wall, the bug-world stand-in for the lost cave bats: harmless, it scatters when disturbed, and frass gathers beneath it to shovel up.
reason: §00 promised it, and it is real: herald moths spend the winter in caves and mines in clusters.

name: Old-world leftovers named in §00
change: Antler chandelier: cut (a hanging chandelier can't be seen well from above, and the candelabra covers old-style light). Bearskin rug: cut (the rug set covers rugs, and a hunting-trophy rug is an odd pride for people who lost the mammals). Dog statue: cut (the cat statue already carries the memory of lost pets).
reason: Remains are allowed (D66), so each is judged on taste and duplication, as §00 promised.

name: Straw Mulch
change: Spread on tilled squares, it keeps them wet for longer, so a mulched bed needs watering less often (how much less is tuned with watering); made from straw in one step.
reason: P11 names it, and real mulch slows the soil drying out; it gives straw its farming job.

name: Cotton Thread
change: Cotton spun on the spinning wheel.
reason: Cotton stays as the owner's leaning (2026-10-01; D15): it needs its own thread to make its own cloth.

name: Cotton Cloth
change: Cotton thread woven at the loom: the finer clothes — the decorative outfits — are made from it, while roughspun cloth makes the everyday ones and silk the finest.
reason: Finer clothes from a finer cloth, so cotton has a job of its own.

name: Purple Dye
change: Ground from wild berries at the dye station; a recipe found at the Butterfly Fields' camp (special colours are found recipes, D26).
reason: Berry dyes are real, though they fade; it gives the berries a job beyond food.

name: Crimson Dye
change: Crushed cochineal at the dye station: the prized red; cloth and outfits dyed with it sell for more. A recipe found at Scorpion Rocks' camp.
reason: Carmine, from cochineal, was among the most valued dyes in Europe; poppy red stays the everyday red.

name: Gall Black
change: Oak galls ground with iron filings at the dye station: the prized, lasting black; dyed cloth and outfits sell for more. A recipe found at the Millipede Forest's camp.
reason: Iron-gall ink was the standard writing ink for over a thousand years; inkcap black stays the everyday black.

name: Oak Gall
change: Chopping an oak sometimes gives one: a growth a tiny gall wasp makes the tree grow around its young.
reason: Real oak galls are made by gall wasps and were the base of black dye and ink — a dye made with a bug's help.

name: Meals and drinks (the new set)
change: The old list is dropped whole (2026-10-01) and this set replaces it: real dishes people cook, from what you grow, fish and farm. Kept as decided (P16, D50, D54): no hunger; a meal heals over a while and gives one boost; a new meal replaces the last; food doesn't spoil; cooking is its own system (D19); the campfire cooks one dish at a time, the wood stove two (it bakes as well), the range several. No dairy, bird eggs or mammal meat (D32): oil is pressed from seeds, honey sweetens, fish sauce seasons. Meals prepare you for a trip — work, fishing or a fight; potions are short and strong, for the moment you need them. One boost per dish, from eight: Stamina (a bigger stamina pool, P14), Sturdy (take a little less damage), Harvest (more from each harvest of crops, fruit and hives), Forage (more from wild plants and mushrooms — the herbalist's food), Fishing (a better catch, sized with the fishing design), Catch (your hand net reaches a square further), Mining (one pickaxe hit fewer on blocks that take two or more) and Swift (walk a little faster). Several things can give the same boost, with a ceiling: however many sources, a block loses at most one hit, and a harvest gains at most one extra from each source. Effort sets the length: a one-ingredient dish lasts about 5 minutes, a cooked dish about 10, a big dish (three or more ingredients, or one made from another made thing) about 20; some dishes make several portions to share. Drinks follow the potions' rule: one boost from a drink at a time. A recipe can take any fish, any grasshopper, locust or cricket, or any fruit — new: the recipe data needs ingredient groups and the stove asks which one to use (recipes take one exact item today). Whole bugs in a dish are small, net-sized ones or brood; big bugs go through the bug extractor as bug meat. Water is free at any station. The General Store sells flour and cornmeal, as it sells salt, so village cooks can bake from the start; the mill grinds your own grain later.
reason: The owner asked for every food to be redone as real dishes cooked from what players grow, fish and farm, with nothing goofy (2026-10-01). Each dish is in the research (docs/product/investigations/research-2026-10-01/foods-real-dishes.md), and the few that adapt a real dish are marked plausible. Learning: a few dishes are known from the start, the plainest stove dishes come with the stove, and the rest are taught by townspeople, sold as recipes, or found.

name: Cornmeal
change: Corn ground at the mill; the General Store sells it too.
reason: The base of polenta, cornbread and the fish fry.

name: Seed Oil
change: Sunflower or pumpkin seeds pressed at the press.
reason: Frying needs oil, and with no animal fat it comes from seeds, as real sunflower and pumpkin-seed oil do.

name: Wood Ash
change: Wood burned at the campfire.
reason: Corn soaked with wood ash makes a dough that holds together for tortillas — the real ash-or-lime soak behind Mexican corn dough.

name: Corn Tortillas
change: Corn and wood ash, made in one step at the wood stove.
reason: The flatbread for tacos; corn is the natural partner of bug protein (tortillas in Mexico, maize porridge in southern Africa).

name: Fish Sauce
change: Any fish and salt, left to ferment in the keg.
reason: The game's savoury seasoning in place of soy sauce: real fish sauce is fish fermented in salt (Cambodia's prahok, Rome's garum).

name: Sourdough Starter
change: Flour and water left in the keg to sour; it raises sourdough bread.
reason: Real sourdough is raised by a starter of flour and water left until wild yeasts take hold.

name: Wood Grub
change: Chopping a dead tree or a fallen log sometimes gives some: beetle larvae that live in rotting wood.
reason: Wood-eating grubs are the real witchetty grubs, roasted in hot ashes; the carrion beetle's grubs stay bug feed, like fly larvae.

name: Corn on the Cob
change: Corn, roasted at the campfire. Boost: Harvest. Known from the start.
reason: The simplest real dish from a village crop.

name: Roasted Seeds
change: Sunflower or pumpkin seeds and salt, roasted at the campfire. Boost: Forage. Known from the start.
reason: Roasted, salted seeds are a real everyday snack.

name: Salt-Grilled Fish
change: Any fish, salt, and sage or thyme, grilled on a skewer at the campfire. Boost: Fishing. Known from the start, since fishing starts in the village (D51).
reason: Japan's salt-grilled fish on a skewer, and fish with sage, a favourite in Italy.

name: Damper
change: Flour and salt, baked in the campfire's coals. Boost: Stamina. Known from the start; the General Store sells the flour.
reason: The Australian campfire bread.

name: Crayfish Boil
change: Crayfish, corn and salt boiled in a pot over the campfire; makes four portions to share. Boost: Sturdy. The Fisherman teaches it; crayfish come in his fish trap.
reason: Louisiana's crawfish boil with corn on the cob, and the Swedish crayfish party.

name: Toasted Grasshoppers
change: Any grasshopper, locust or cricket, toasted with salt. Boost: Stamina. Taught in the western town, where the locusts are.
reason: Chapulines, an everyday food in Oaxaca, Mexico.

name: Ash-Roasted Grubs
change: Wood grubs roasted in the campfire's hot ashes. Boost: Mining. The Bug Dealer teaches it.
reason: Witchetty grubs, a staple insect food of the Australian desert, roasted in hot ashes.

name: Smoked Fish
change: Any fish, salted and smoked over the campfire. Boost: Stamina — food for a long trip. The Fisherman teaches it.
reason: Salted, smoked fish is a real food that keeps a long time.

name: Polenta
change: Cornmeal and salt. Boost: Stamina. Comes with the wood stove.
reason: Italy's polenta and Africa's maize porridge (ugali, sadza).

name: Pumpkin Soup
change: Pumpkin, sage and seed oil. Boost: Harvest. Comes with the wood stove.
reason: A real everyday soup; sage and pumpkin are a classic pair.

name: Mushroom Soup
change: Brown mushrooms or chanterelles and cabbage. Boost: Forage. Comes with the wood stove; the village's ready meal (D19's place).
reason: Mushrooms went into Russian cabbage soup; the brown mushroom really grows on compost.

name: Honey Carrots
change: Carrots and plums stewed with honey. Boost: Swift. The Beekeeper teaches it.
reason: Tzimmes, the honeyed carrot dish of the Jewish New Year (made with dried plums; fresh ones here).

name: Eggplant and Tomato Stew
change: Eggplant, tomato and thyme in seed oil. Boost: Harvest. The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: Plausible: eggplant and tomato stewed in oil with thyme, the heart of ratatouille without its onion and garlic.

name: Sautéed Chanterelles
change: Chanterelles fried in seed oil. Boost: Forage. A recipe found in the Millipede Forest.
reason: Chanterelles really are fried in fat, which carries their flavour.

name: Fried Crickets
change: Crickets, seed oil and salt. Boost: Sturdy. The Bug Dealer teaches it.
reason: An everyday snack in Thailand, which has about 20,000 cricket farms.

name: Battered Grasshoppers
change: Any grasshopper or locust in a flour batter, fried in seed oil. Boost: Catch. Taught in the western town.
reason: Indonesia's rempeyek, grasshoppers and crickets fried crisp in a light batter.

name: Wasp Larvae in Honey
change: Wasp larvae simmered with honey and fish sauce. Boost: Harvest. The Beekeeper teaches it.
reason: Plausible: Japan's hachinoko simmers wasp larvae in soy sauce and sugar; fish sauce and honey stand in.

name: Ant Egg Soup
change: Ant eggs, mint and fish sauce. Boost: Mining. The Myrmecologist teaches it.
reason: The red-ant-egg soup of Laos and north-east Thailand (made there with weaver ants).

name: Cornmeal-Fried Fish
change: Any fish in a cornmeal coat, fried in seed oil. Boost: Sturdy. The Fisherman teaches it.
reason: The American fish fry.

name: Clear Fish Soup (Ukha)
change: Any fish, carrot and fennel. Boost: Fishing, a big dish. The Fisherman teaches it.
reason: Russian ukha, a clear soup of freshwater fish.

name: Caterpillar Stew
change: Silk-moth caterpillars and tomato, served on polenta. Boost: Stamina, a big dish. Taught at the Butterfly Fields' camp.
reason: Southern Africa's mopane worms — emperor-moth caterpillars — stewed with tomato and eaten with maize porridge. Milkweed caterpillars stay off the menu: in reality they carry the plant's poison.

name: Bug-Meat Stew
change: Bug meat, pumpkin, carrot, cabbage and fish sauce. Boost: Sturdy, a big dish. The Bug Dealer teaches it.
reason: Plausible: built on the insect stews eaten with porridge in southern Africa; it is where the extractor's meat goes.

name: Tacos
change: Corn tortillas, cabbage and tomato, with toasted grasshoppers, ant eggs or fish. Boost: Stamina, a big dish. Taught in the western town.
reason: Mexican tacos of grasshoppers, of ant brood (escamoles) and of fish are all real.

name: Sourdough Bread
change: Sourdough starter, flour and salt, baked at the wood stove. Boost: Stamina, a big dish. The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: Real sourdough, raised by its starter.

name: Seeded Cornbread
change: Cornmeal, sunflower seeds and berries, baked at the wood stove. Boost: Forage, a big dish. Taught in the western town.
reason: Cherokee and Seneca cooks bake cornbread with sunflower seeds and berries.

name: Baked Apples
change: Apples and honey, baked at the wood stove. Boost: Harvest. The Beekeeper teaches it.
reason: A real everyday dish; honey is one of the usual sweeteners.

name: Cricket Bread
change: Flour and toasted crickets, baked at the wood stove. Boost: Mining, a big dish. The Bug Dealer teaches it.
reason: A real modern bread sold in Finland, with cricket flour in the dough.

name: Fruit Spread
change: Apples or plums cooked down for hours at the wood stove; no dairy, and no sweetener needed. Boost: Swift. The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: Apple butter and plum butter (powidl) are real; 'butter' there means only a thick spread, so the game calls it a spread.

name: Sauerkraut
change: Cabbage, salt and carrot, left to ferment in the keg. Boost: Sturdy. The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: Real sauerkraut keeps for months with no cold store.

name: Mint Tea
change: Mint steeped at the campfire; a drink, about 5 minutes. Boost: Swift. Known from the start.
reason: A real herbal tea.

name: Chamomile Tea
change: Chamomile steeped at the campfire; a drink, about 5 minutes. Boost: Catch (a calm, steady hand). The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: A real calming tea; chamomile is common in the village.

name: Dandelion Coffee
change: Roasted dandelion root brewed at the campfire; a drink, about 5 minutes. Boost: Stamina. The General Store sells the recipe.
reason: A real coffee substitute, long before the western town's coffee beans.

name: Fruit Kompot
change: Any fruit boiled with honey at the wood stove; a drink, about 10 minutes. Boost: Harvest. Comes with the wood stove.
reason: Eastern Europe's kompot, a way to keep fruit for winter.

name: Fruit Juice
change: Any fruit at the press; a drink, about 5 minutes. Boost: Swift.
reason: The press's first job, and the start of cider.

name: Cider
change: Apple juice fermented in the keg. Heals a little; no boost; sells well. Maren's brewing room teaches it.
reason: Real cider; fruit gets a second use as a trade good.

name: Mead
change: Honey and water fermented in the keg. Heals a little; no boost; sells well. Maren's brewing room teaches it.
reason: Real mead, perhaps the oldest fermented drink; honey gets a trade good.
